question: When an unreceipted legacy `runs.json` exists beside a non-empty canonical `subagent_runs` table, should doctor permanently suppress automatic import while preserving and warning about the source?
rationale: Both automatic merging and permanent skipping can change user-visible persisted run state; source inspection and tests can prove mechanics but cannot choose the intended upgrade and recovery contract.

options.title: Approve skip and preserve
options.body: Keep the PR's fail-safe behavior: record a durable skipped receipt, preserve the JSON source, warn the operator, and never merge it automatically.

options.title: Add explicit recovery flow
options.body: Require a deliberate doctor recovery command or guided action that lets an operator inspect and import selected preserved records without restoring them automatically.

options.title: Retain automatic compatibility
options.body: Keep a compatibility import path despite the demonstrated resurrection risk, with additional conflict policy and upgrade tests.

recommendation.title: Approve skip and preserve
recommendation.body: Keep the PR's fail-safe behavior: record a durable skipped receipt, preserve the JSON source, warn the operator, and never merge it automatically.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged SQLite migration and recovery work is the closest available ownership signal for this compatibility choice.
